title: Thanksgiving
definition: Thanksgiving is the believer’s grateful response to God’s grace, provision, mercy, and faithfulness in Christ.
summary: Thanksgiving is the believer’s grateful response to God’s grace, provision, mercy, and faithfulness in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus reveals the generosity of God, and through Him believers learn to give thanks in all circumstances without denying hardship.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Thanksgiving is not pretending life is painless. It is recognizing God’s goodness and faithfulness even when circumstances are difficult.

Scripture calls believers to give thanks because grace has already been given in Christ. Gratitude grows as the heart remembers God’s mercy.

The Holy Spirit helps believers see gifts they might overlook and turns remembrance into worship. Thanksgiving becomes a way of resisting bitterness and despair.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Pain can narrow the heart until only loss is visible. Thanksgiving helps believers remember that suffering is real but not ultimate.

This doctrine also challenges entitlement. Everything good is mercy, and every mercy should lead back to the Giver.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Practice thanksgiving by naming specific evidences of God’s grace. Thank Him for Christ, for daily provision, for sustaining mercy, and for the Spirit’s help even in weakness.
